newsitem.title: USA: KCBT July wheat sets new 10-1/2-month high.
newsitem.headline: KCBT July wheat sets new 10-1/2-month high.

text.p: KCBT new-crop July wheat surged to a new 10-1/2-month high by midsession on escalating concerns that a large amount of wheat was lost during last week's freeze in the U.S. Great Plains, traders said.

July jumped to a session high of $4.80 per bushel by midsession, the highest level for that month since $4.80 was notched on May 28, 1996. The contract high for July is $4.99 which was set on April 22, 1996.
Crop experts Friday again expressed ideas that a lot of wheat has been damaged.

Last week's freeze may have sliced more than 100 million bushels from the Kansas wheat crop and severe losses in Oklahoma also were likely, said crop specialists in those states. In Kansas alone, last week's freeze may have cut production 100 million to 150 million bushels.

"Those numbers for Kansas alone are not unrealistic," said Rollie Sears, a Kansas State University wheat breeder, who this week toured the damaged areas. "The damage in the southern third of the state is worse than I thought."
Thursday's EU decision to halt the EU's weekly wheat export tenders amid mounting concerns about dry weather plus a forecast for more dry weather in France boosted prices.
French weather forecasters Friday predicted another five days without rain across most of the country's farm districts.
At 1145 CDT, KCBT wheat was up 13 to 15 cents, with May up 13 cents at $4.95 and July 14-1/4 higher at $3.77 a bushel.
